name: Residence Visa
description: The F-2 visa provides long-term residence status in Korea with greater freedom than employment visas. It's available through various subcategories including points-based, spouse, and investor routes.
keyRequirement: Points-based assessment (80+) or family ties to Korean citizen
targetAudience: Spouses of Korean citizens or residents

eligibility.label: F-2-7 (Points System): Score 80+ points
eligibility.description: Based on age, education, Korean ability, income, etc.

eligibility.label: F-2-1: Married to Korean citizen
eligibility.description: Must be legally married with registered marriage

eligibility.label: Usually requires prior legal residence
eligibility.description: Most F-2 categories require existing visa history

incomeRequirement.notes: F-2-7 requires income above GNI average (approximately ₩40-50 million/year)

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must be valid for duration of requested stay

documents.name: Current Alien Registration Card
documents.description: Your current ARC showing valid visa status

documents.name: Points Calculation Worksheet (F-2-7)
documents.description: Self-assessment of points across all categories

documents.name: Income Tax Documents
documents.description: Tax payment certificates from Korean tax office

documents.name: Employment Certificate
documents.description: Letter from employer confirming position and salary

applicationSteps.title: Check Eligibility & Calculate Points
applicationSteps.description: Determine which F-2 subcategory fits your situation. For F-2-7, calculate your points.

applicationSteps.title: Gather Supporting Documents
applicationSteps.description: Collect all documents that prove your points claims or eligibility.
tips: Get official TOPIK certificate if needed

applicationSteps.title: Submit Application
applicationSteps.description: Visit immigration office with all documents.

applicationSteps.title: Receive F-2 Status
applicationSteps.description: Get new ARC with F-2 visa status.

processingTime.notes: May take longer if interview required or additional documents needed

workPermission.notes: F-2 provides much more work flexibility than employment-tied visas

faqs.question: What is the F-2-7 points system?
faqs.answer: F-2-7 uses a points system based on: Age (max 25), Education (max 35), Korean proficiency/TOPIK (max 20), Income (max 25), Experience in Korea (max 10), and Social integration course completion (max 5). You need 80+ points total.

faqs.question: Can I work for any company on F-2?
faqs.answer: Yes! Unlike E-7 which ties you to one employer, F-2 allows you to work for any company or be self-employed without visa changes.

faqs.question: How long do I need to stay in Korea to qualify for F-2-7?
faqs.answer: You typically need 2-3 years of legal residence on another visa (like E-7) before qualifying for F-2-7.

faqs.question: Can F-2 lead to permanent residence (F-5)?
faqs.answer: Yes. After 2+ years on F-2, you may be eligible for F-5 permanent residence, depending on your continued eligibility and contribution to Korea.

faqs.question: What happens if I lose my job on F-2?
faqs.answer: Unlike E-7, losing your job doesn't affect your F-2 status. You can take time to find new employment without visa concerns.

tips: Start preparing for F-2-7 early - take TOPIK, build work history
TOPIK Level 5-6 gives significant points boost
Track your income - higher income = more points
Complete KIIP (social integration) courses for bonus points
Keep all tax and employment records organized
Consider timing - some points categories have age limits
warnings: Points must be verifiable - don't exaggerate
Maintain continuous residence - long absences may affect status
Must still report address changes to immigration

pathsFrom.name: Professional Employment Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Score 80+ on the F-2-7 points system. Typically need 3+ years on E-7, TOPIK Level 4+, income above GNI average, and other qualifying factors.
pathsFrom.notes: The most common path to F-2. Start building your points early: take TOPIK (Level 5-6 gives big boost), maintain high income, and consider completing KIIP social integration courses for bonus points.

pathsFrom.name: Intra-Company Transfer Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Meet F-2-7 points requirements (80+). Extended residence in Korea on D-7 counts toward experience points.
pathsFrom.notes: D-7 holders with long tenure in Korea can accumulate enough points for F-2-7, especially if they invest in Korean language skills.

pathsFrom.name: Corporate Investment Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Meet F-2-99 investment criteria or F-2-7 points system (80+). Business must be operational and profitable.
pathsFrom.notes: D-8 holders can qualify through the investment route (F-2-99) or the standard points system (F-2-7). Successful business operations strengthen your application.

pathsFrom.name: Overseas Korean Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Meet F-2 eligibility through ethnic Korean status plus additional criteria depending on subcategory.
pathsFrom.notes: F-4 holders may transition to F-2 for additional stability or as a stepping stone to F-5 permanent residence.

pathsFrom.name: Marriage Migration Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Meet F-2 eligibility. F-6 holders married to Korean citizens may qualify through marriage-based subcategories.
pathsFrom.notes: F-6 holders may transition to F-2 for greater independence, especially after extended residence in Korea.
